derivations.claim: For an interior face $F=K|L$, the shared-flux definitions give $Q_{K,F}(u)+Q_{L,F}(u)=T_F(u_K-u_L)+T_F(u_L-u_K)=0$. Thus summing cell balances cancels every interior flux exactly.

In $\sum_K |K|v_K(A_hu)_K$, the two terms contributed by an interior face are $T_F[v_K(u_K-u_L)+v_L(u_L-u_K)]=T_F(v_K-v_L)(u_K-u_L)$. A boundary face contributes $T_{K,F}v_Ku_K$. Summing all faces proves the displayed identity.

Set $v=u$ in step 1.2. The resulting stiffness quadratic form is a sum of nonnegative terms. If it is zero, every interior term forces $u_K=u_L$, and every boundary term forces $u_K=0$ on its incident cell. The path condition [A1] propagates these zeros through the connected cell graph, so $u=0$. The finite-dimensional symmetric stiffness matrix therefore has trivial kernel and is positive definite and invertible. Since the volume matrix $M_h=\operatorname{diag}(|K|)$ is invertible, $A_h=M_h^{-1}(M_hA_h)$ is also invertible; inhomogeneous boundary values change only the right-hand side.

Suppose $u$ solves the cell balances with $f_K\ge0$ and $g_F\ge0$. If a cell value has a negative global minimum, choose a minimizing cell $K$. Every interior summand $T_F(u_K-u_L)$ in its balance is nonpositive, and every boundary summand $T_{K,F}(u_K-g_F)$ is strictly negative. Since the balance equals $|K|f_K\ge0$, all summands must be zero. Thus the minimum propagates unchanged to every adjacent cell along a path from [A1], but at a boundary face the summand $T_{K,F}(u_K-g_F)$ is strictly negative. This contradiction rules out a negative minimum, so all cell values are nonnegative.

derivations.claim: Fix a cell $K$. Traverse its supplied path to a boundary face. The signed increments telescope from $u_K$ to the terminal boundary value $0$, so $u_K=\sum_{e\in\gamma_K}\epsilon_{K,e}\Delta_eu$, where each $\epsilon_{K,e}\in\{-1,1\}$ records the orientation.

Let $\mathcal T$ be a cell-face mesh as in [[def-fv-admissible-cell-face-mesh]], with $x_K$ the volume centroid of each cell and $x_F$ the face centroid. For the mimetic branch require the following explicit face-moment closure on each cell:
$$ \sum_{F\subset\partial K}|F|n_{K,F}=0,\qquad \sum_{F\subset\partial K}|F|x_F\otimes n_{K,F}=|K|I_d. $$
Here $I_d$ is the identity matrix on $\mathbb R^d$ and $(x\otimes n)_{ij}=x_i n_j$. These are finite geometric checks on the face data; they impose no center-to-face orthogonality. For every cell use one real cell-mean unknown $u_K$; for every face use one shared real face-mean unknown $u_F$. On a boundary face $F\subset\partial\Omega$, the value $u_F=g_F$ is prescribed. Write $n_{K,F}$ for the outward unit normal. Define the reconstructed cell gradient and its face residual by
$$ G_Ku=\frac1{|K|}\sum_{F\subset\partial K}|F|u_Fn_{K,F},\qquad \rho_{K,F}(u)=u_F-u_K-G_Ku\cdot(x_F-x_K). $$
Interpret $u_K$ and $u_F$ as cell and face averages. For a symmetric positive-definite tensor $A_K$ constant on $K$ (so $z\cdot A_Kz>0$ for every nonzero $z$), define
$$ \mathscr A_K(u,v)=|K|(A_KG_Ku)\cdot G_Kv+\lambda_{\min}(A_K)\sum_{F\subset\partial K}\frac{|F|}{d_{K,F}}\rho_{K,F}(u)\rho_{K,F}(v), $$
where $\lambda_{\min}(A_K)>0$ is the smallest eigenvalue of $A_K$. The **linear hybrid mimetic scheme** with homogeneous Dirichlet data is to find all cell and interior-face values $u$ such that
$$ \sum_{K\in\mathcal K}\mathscr A_K(u,v)=\sum_{K\in\mathcal K}v_K\int_K f(x)\,dx $$
for every test vector $v$ whose boundary face values are zero. For each local face $F\subset\partial K$, let $\phi_{K,F}$ have face value $1$ on $F$, zero on the other faces of $K$, and cell value zero. Define the outward numerical flux $Q_{K,F}(u)=-\mathscr A_K(u,\phi_{K,F})$.

There is also a monotone $p$-growth backward-Euler extension, specified as an algebraic scheme but with no existence or convergence claim in this definition. Let $1<p<\infty$, set $p'=p/(p-1)$, and let $a(x,\xi)$ be a **Carathéodory flux**, meaning that $x\mapsto a(x,\xi)$ is measurable for each fixed $\xi$ and $\xi\mapsto a(x,\xi)$ is continuous for almost every $x$. Assume there are constants $C,\alpha>0$, a nonnegative $g\in L^{p'}(\Omega)$, and a nonnegative $h\in L^1(\Omega)$ such that, outside one null set,
$$ |a(x,\xi)|\le C(g(x)+|\xi|^{p-1}),\qquad a(x,\xi)\cdot\xi\ge\alpha|\xi|^p-h(x),\qquad (a(x,\xi)-a(x,\eta))\cdot(\xi-\eta)\ge0. $$
For each cell set $b_K(\xi)=|K|^{-1}\int_Ka(x,\xi)\,dx$, and fix $\alpha_{0,K}>0$. Put $\psi_p(s)=|s|^{p-2}s$ for $s\ne0$ and $\psi_p(0)=0$. Its spatial operator, linear in the test vector $v$, is
$$ \mathcal A_{h,K}(u;v)=|K|b_K(G_Ku)\cdot G_Kv+\alpha_{0,K}\sum_{F\subset\partial K}\frac{|F|}{d_{K,F}^{p-1}}\psi_p(\rho_{K,F}(u))\rho_{K,F}(v). $$
For this extension define $Q_{K,F}^{\rm nl}(u)=-\mathcal A_{h,K}(u;\phi_{K,F})$.
On a time partition $0=t_0<\cdots<t_N=T$, given $u^{n-1}$ and $f\in L^{p'}((0,T)\times\Omega)$, put $f_K^n=((t_n-t_{n-1})|K|)^{-1}\int_{t_{n-1}}^{t_n}\int_K f$. The backward-Euler step seeks $u^n$ with zero boundary face values satisfying
$$ \sum_{K\in\mathcal K}|K|\frac{u_K^n-u_K^{n-1}}{t_n-t_{n-1}}v_K+\sum_{K\in\mathcal K}\mathcal A_{h,K}(u^n;v)=\sum_{K\in\mathcal K}|K|f_K^n v_K $$
for every test vector with zero boundary face values. The formula specifies a candidate discrete method; solvability and convergence require separate results.

For an affine function $\ell(x)=b\cdot x+c$, its cell and face averages satisfy $G_K\ell=b$ and $\rho_{K,F}(\ell)=0$ by the displayed face-moment closure. The drawing illustrates the cell and face degrees of freedom on a skew cell; no center-to-face orthogonality is assumed.

```tikz

  \draw[thick] (0,0) -- (2,0) -- (3,1) -- (1,1) -- cycle;
  \fill (1.5,0.5) circle (2pt) node[below] {$u_K$};
  \fill (1,0) circle (2pt) node[below] {$u_{F_1}$};
  \fill (2.5,0.5) circle (2pt) node[right] {$u_{F_2}$};
  \fill (2,1) circle (2pt) node[above] {$u_{F_3}$};
  \fill (0.5,0.5) circle (2pt) node[left] {$u_{F_4}$};
  \draw[->,blue] (1.5,0.5) -- (2.2,0.5) node[right] {$G_Ku$};
\end{tikzpicture}
```

Neither specification by itself proves solvability, a conforming $W_0^{1,p}$ reconstruction, or a mesh-uniform discrete Aubin–Lions estimate; those require separate results or hypotheses.

derivations.claim: For an affine $\ell(x)=b\cdot x+c$, the cell and face means are $\ell_K=\ell(x_K)$ and $\ell_F=\ell(x_F)$. The first face-moment identity annihilates the constant term in $G_K\ell$; the transpose of the second identity is $\sum_F|F|n_{K,F}\otimes x_F=|K|I_d$, so $G_K\ell=b$. Hence $\rho_{K,F}(\ell)=\ell_F-\ell_K-b\cdot(x_F-x_K)=0$.

For arbitrary $v$, [A1] gives $|K|(A_KG_Kv)\cdot G_Kv\ge\lambda_{\min}(A_K)|K||G_Kv|^2$. The stabilization coefficient is $\lambda_{\min}(A_K)>0$, so summing its squared residual terms gives $\mathscr A_K(v,v)\ge\lambda_{\min}(A_K)\|v\|_{K,\mathrm{mim}}^2$.

For the nonlinear flux, the cell average preserves monotonicity because $(b_K(\xi)-b_K(\eta))\cdot(\xi-\eta)=\frac1{|K|}\int_K(a(x,\xi)-a(x,\eta))\cdot(\xi-\eta)\,dx\ge0.$ The pointwise bounds in [A2] also give $b_K(\xi)\cdot\xi\ge\alpha|\xi|^p-|K|^{-1}\int_Kh$ and $|b_K(\xi)|\le C(|K|^{-1}\int_Kg+|\xi|^{p-1})$. Thus the averaged flux retains monotonicity, coercivity, and $p$-growth.

The global form is symmetric because each $A_K$ is symmetric and the residual term is a symmetric product. If its energy at $v$ is zero, step 1.2 forces $G_Kv=0$ and every $\rho_{K,F}(v)=0$. The latter then gives $v_F=v_K$ on every face. Shared face values make all adjacent cell values equal, and a boundary face has prescribed value zero; boundary anchoring propagates this zero to every cell. Thus the homogeneous matrix has trivial kernel. It is square and finite-dimensional, so it is invertible and positive definite; every cell-source vector has a unique solution.

For an interior face $F=K|L$, the global equation tested by its shared face basis function gives $\mathscr A_K(u,\phi_{K,F})+\mathscr A_L(u,\phi_{L,F})=0$, hence $Q_{K,F}+Q_{L,F}=0$. For a cell basis $\phi_K$, the equation gives $\mathscr A_K(u,\phi_K)=\int_Kf$. The local constant vector $\mathbf1_K=\phi_K+\sum_{F\subset\partial K}\phi_{K,F}$ has zero reconstructed gradient by the first face-moment identity and zero residual; therefore $\mathscr A_K(u,\mathbf1_K)=0$. Expanding this identity and using the cell equation yields $\sum_{F\subset\partial K}Q_{K,F}=\int_Kf$.

If $u$ is the face and cell averages of an affine $\ell$, step 1.1 gives $G_Ku=b$ and all residuals of $u$ vanish. For the local face basis, $G_K\phi_{K,F}=|F|n_{K,F}/|K|$. Thus $\mathscr A_K(u,\phi_{K,F})=|F|(A_Kb)\cdot n_{K,F}$, and the definition $Q_{K,F}=-\mathscr A_K(u,\phi_{K,F})$ gives the exact outward diffusive flux.

The scalar map $\psi_p(s)=|s|^{p-2}s$ is increasing: it is increasing on each half-line by monotonicity of $r\mapsto r^{p-1}$ for $r\ge0$, and its values are nonpositive on $s\le0$ and nonnegative on $s\ge0$. Hence $(\psi_p(r)-\psi_p(s))(r-s)\ge0$. For any two states $u,v$, the difference $\mathcal A_{h,K}(u;u-v)-\mathcal A_{h,K}(v;u-v)$ is the sum of $|K|(b_K(G_Ku)-b_K(G_Kv))\cdot(G_Ku-G_Kv)$ and the nonnegative residual terms $\alpha_{0,K}|F|d_{K,F}^{1-p}(\psi_p(\rho_{K,F}(u))-\psi_p(\rho_{K,F}(v)))(\rho_{K,F}(u)-\rho_{K,F}(v))$. Step 1.3 and scalar monotonicity make every term nonnegative. Testing with $v=u$ and using the coercivity bound in [A2] yields $\mathcal A_{h,K}(u;u)\ge |K|\left(\alpha|G_Ku|^p-|K|^{-1}\int_Kh\right)+\alpha_{0,K}\sum_F\frac{|F|}{d_{K,F}^{p-1}}|\rho_{K,F}(u)|^p.$ For a fixed state, the local constant test vector has zero gradient and residual, so the spatial form annihilates it. A shared interior-face test in an implicit step makes $Q_{K,F}^{\rm nl}+Q_{L,F}^{\rm nl}=0$. Testing the step equation by the cell basis gives $\mathcal A_{h,K}(u^n;\phi_K)=|K|f_K^n-|K|(u_K^n-u_K^{n-1})/\tau_n$. Expanding the zero constant-test identity gives $\sum_FQ_{K,F}^{\rm nl}=|K|f_K^n-|K|(u_K^n-u_K^{n-1})/\tau_n$, the local balance with accumulation.

Let $\mathcal T$ be a finite TPFA-admissible cell-face mesh, let every cell be connected through interior faces to a cell with a boundary face, and let $T_F>0$ be the transmissibilities of [[def-tpfa-harmonic-face-scheme]]. For cell vectors $u,v$, define
$$ (A_hu)_K=\frac1{|K|}\left(\sum_{F=K|L}T_F(u_K-u_L)+\sum_{F\subset\partial K\cap\partial\Omega}T_{K,F}u_K\right). $$
Then interior fluxes are locally conservative, and for all cell vectors $u,v$,
$$ \sum_{K\in\mathcal K}|K|v_K(A_hu)_K= \sum_{F=K|L\in\mathcal F_{\rm int}}T_F(v_K-v_L)(u_K-u_L) +\sum_{F\in\mathcal F_{\rm bdy}}T_{K,F}v_Ku_K. $$
The stiffness matrix associated with the displayed bilinear identity is symmetric positive definite. Equivalently, $A_h$ is self-adjoint and positive definite in the volume-weighted inner product $\langle u,v\rangle_h=\sum_K|K|u_Kv_K$; its ordinary coordinate matrix need not be symmetric when cell volumes differ. Hence every finite source and boundary-data vector gives a unique solution. If all cell sources and all prescribed boundary face values are nonnegative, then every solution cell value is nonnegative. The maximum-principle claim uses the boundary anchor; no diagonal sign statement alone is used as a substitute for that condition.

derivations.claim: For each face orient the exact flux $J_F$ outward from one incident cell, and set $\delta_F=Q_{K,F}(I_hu)-J_F$; on a boundary face set $\delta_F=Q_{K,F}(I_hu)-J_{K,F}$. Let $y_F$ be the intersection of the center-normal line with an interior face and the orthogonal projection point on a boundary face. Taylor's theorem along the normal gives, on $F=K|L$ with $n=n_{K,F}$, $u(x_K)=u(y_F)-d_{K,F}\partial_nu_K(y_F)+r_K,\quad u(x_L)=u(y_F)+d_{L,F}\partial_nu_L(y_F)+r_L,$ where $|r_K|+|r_L|\le C M h^2$. By [A1], $\lambda_K\partial_nu_K(y_F)=\lambda_L\partial_nu_L(y_F)=s_F$. Substitution into the harmonic formula gives $Q_{K,F}(I_hu)=-|F|s_F+T_F(r_K-r_L)$. The face trace varies by at most $M h$ from $y_F$, so $|J_{K,F}+|F|s_F|\le C\lambda^*M|F|h$. Since [F1]–[F2] imply $T_F\le C|F|/h$, we obtain $|\delta_F|\le C M|F|h$. On a boundary face, $u(y_F)=0$ and the one-sided Taylor expansion $u(x_K)=-d_{K,F}\partial_nu_K(y_F)+r_K$ yields the same bound for $\delta_F$.

By uniform regularity, every transmissibility satisfies $T_F\ge c|F|/h$. There are at most $N_0$ faces per cell, $|F|\le Ch^{d-1}$, and $|K|\ge ch^d$, so $\#\mathcal K_h\le |\Omega|/(ch^d)$ and $\sum_F|F|\le C h^{-1}$. Step 1.1 therefore gives $\sum_F\frac{\delta_F^2}{T_F}\le C M^2h^3\sum_F|F|\le C M^2h^2.$ Thus the vector of local flux defects has transmissibility-dual norm at most $C hM$.

Let $e=U_h-I_hu$. The exact cell balances in [A1] and the finite-volume balances for $U_h$ imply, for every cell vector $v$, $a_h(e,v)=-\sum_{F\in\mathcal F_{\rm int}}\delta_F(v_K-v_L)-\sum_{F\in\mathcal F_{\rm bdy}}\delta_Fv_K,$ because the two exact interior fluxes are oppositely oriented. Take $v=e$. Weighted Cauchy–Schwarz gives $\|e\|_{E_h}^2\le(\sum_F\delta_F^2/T_F)^{1/2}\|e\|_{E_h}$. If $e=0$ the first estimate is immediate; otherwise divide by $\|e\|_{E_h}$ and use step 2.1 to obtain $\|e\|_{E_h}\le ChM$. The bilinear identity used here is [F3].

Let $V$ be a separable reflexive real Banach space, let $H$ be a real Hilbert
space, and let $i:V\to H$ be an injective continuous linear map with dense
range. Let $V^*$ be the continuous real dual of $V$ and write
$\langle\cdot,\cdot\rangle_{V^*,V}$ for its pairing with $V$. The canonical
map $J:H\to V^*$ is
$$J h(v)=(h,iv)_H\qquad(h\in H,\ v\in V).$$
It is continuous because $|Jh(v)|\le \|h\|_H\|i\|\|v\|_V$, and injective
because $i(V)$ is dense in $H$. A triple $(V,H,J)$ with these properties is
a **Banach evolution triple**. If $V$ is Hilbert, this is the real evolution
triple of [[def-parabolic-evolution-triple-and-energy-space]].

For $1<p<\infty$, $L^p(0,T;V)$ denotes the Bochner space of strongly
measurable $V$-valued functions with finite $p$th power norm, and
$p'=p/(p-1)$. For $u\in L^p(0,T;V)$ and $g\in L^{p'}(0,T;V^*)$, say
$g=u'$ in the distributional time sense if
$$\int_0^T (iu(t),iv)_H\,\phi'(t)\,dt =-\int_0^T\langle g(t),v\rangle_{V^*,V}\,\phi(t)\,dt$$
for every $v\in V$ and $\phi\in C_c^\infty(0,T)$. Define
$$W_p(0,T;V)=\{u\in L^p(0,T;V):u'\in L^{p'}(0,T;V^*)\}.$$
This definition assigns no endpoint values; a separate chain-rule theorem is
needed before evaluating a function in this space at an endpoint.

Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]).

Let $d\ge1$, let $\Omega\subset\mathbb R^d$ be a bounded open set, and
let $1<p<\infty$ satisfy $p>\max(1,2d/(d+2))$. Put
$V=W_0^{1,p}(\Omega;\mathbb R)$ with norm
$\|v\|_V=\|\nabla v\|_{L^p(\Omega)}$, $H=L^2(\Omega;\mathbb R)$, and
$p'=p/(p-1)$. The Poincaré inequality makes this norm equivalent to the full
$W^{1,p}$ norm. [[lem-pe12-w0p-separable-reflexive]] gives separability and
reflexivity, while [[lem-pe12-w1p-compact-l2-embedding]] gives the dense
continuous compact inclusion $V\Subset H$; these are the hypotheses of the
evolution triple in [[def-pe12-gelfand-triple]]. The compact-inclusion result
uses the stated threshold also when $d=1$, where it reduces to $p>1$.

A measurable flux $a:\Omega\times\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R^d$ is an admissible
**coercive monotone diffusion flux of p-growth** if it is Carathéodory (for
each $\xi$, $x\mapsto a(x,\xi)$ is measurable, and for almost every $x$,
$\xi\mapsto a(x,\xi)$ is continuous), and there are constants $C<\infty$,
$\alpha>0$, nonnegative functions $g\in L^{p'}(\Omega)$ and
$h\in L^1(\Omega)$, and one
null set outside which, for all $\xi,\eta\in\mathbb R^d$,
$$|a(x,\xi)|\le C\bigl(g(x)+|\xi|^{p-1}\bigr),\qquad a(x,\xi)\cdot\xi\ge\alpha|\xi|^p-h(x),$$
$$\bigl(a(x,\xi)-a(x,\eta)\bigr)\cdot(\xi-\eta)\ge0.$$
The induced operator $A:V\to V^*$ is
$$\langle A(v),w\rangle_{V^*,V} =\int_\Omega a(x,\nabla v(x))\cdot\nabla w(x)\,dx.$$
The growth bound and Hölder's inequality make this pairing finite and give
$\|A(v)\|_{V^*}\le C_1(\|g\|_{p'}+\|v\|_V^{p-1})$ for a constant $C_1$.
The finite-dimensional test-coordinate continuity used in the backward Euler
existence argument follows from the stated Carathéodory and growth conditions
by dominated convergence, as proved in
[[thm-pe12-backward-euler-galerkin-existence-energy]]. No additional global
operator-continuity hypothesis is imposed.

For $f\in L^{p'}(0,T;V^*)$, a weak evolution solution is a function
$u\in W_p(0,T;V)\cap L^\infty(0,T;H)$ with a continuous $H$ representative
such that $u'+A(u)=f$ in $L^{p'}(0,T;V^*)$ and $u(0)=u_0\in H$.

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let
$\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^d$ be bounded and open, $d\ge1$, let
$1<p<\infty$, and let $0<T<\infty$. Put $V=W_0^{1,p}(\Omega;\mathbb R)$ with gradient norm
$\|v\|_V=\|\nabla v\|_{L^p}$, and suppose $V$ has a continuous inclusion in
a real Hilbert space $H$. If $u_j$ is bounded in $L^p(0,T;V)$ and its image
in $L^p(0,T;H)$ converges strongly to $u$, then a subsequence converges
weakly in $L^p(0,T;V)$ to some $U$, the image of $U$ equals $u$, and
$\nabla u_j\rightharpoonup\nabla U$ in
$L^p((0,T)\times\Omega;\mathbb R^d)$.

Assume the Axiom of Choice.

Let $Q=(0,T)\times\Omega$ have finite measure, $1<p<\infty$, and let
$a(x,\xi)$ be a Carathéodory flux with the monotonicity and $p$-growth
hypotheses of [[def-pe12-monotone-diffusion-flux]], independent of time.
Suppose $\xi_n\rightharpoonup\xi$ in $L^p(Q;\mathbb R^d)$,
$q_n=a(x,\xi_n)\rightharpoonup q$ in $L^{p'}(Q;\mathbb R^d)$, and
$$\limsup_{n\to\infty}\int_Q q_n\cdot\xi_n \le\int_Qq\cdot\xi.$$
Then $q(x,t)=a(x,\xi(x,t))$ for almost every $(t,x)\in Q$.

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let
$(V,H,J)$ be the Banach evolution triple of
[[def-pe12-gelfand-triple]], let $1<p<\infty$, and suppose
$u\in L^p(0,T;V)$ with distributional derivative
$u'\in L^{p'}(0,T;V^*)$. Then $u$ has a unique representative in
$C([0,T];H)$ and, for every $0\le s\le t\le T$,
$$\|u(t)\|_H^2-\|u(s)\|_H^2 =2\int_s^t\langle u'(r),u(r)\rangle_{V^*,V}\,dr.$$

Assume the Axiom of Choice for the ACL and absolutely-continuous
fundamental-theorem interfaces. Let $I\subseteq\mathbb R$ be a nonempty open
interval, let $1\le p\le\infty$, let $\mathbb K\in\{\mathbb R,\mathbb C\}$,
and let $u\in W^{1,p}(I;\mathbb K)$, with weak derivative class $Du$. Then
there is exactly one continuous representative $u^*$ of the class of $u$ on
$I$ that is locally absolutely continuous, that is, absolutely continuous on
every compact interval contained in $I$, and satisfies
$$u^*(x)-u^*(y)=\int_y^xDu(t)\,dt\qquad\text{for every }x,y\in I,$$
where for $x<y$ the right-hand side denotes $-\int_x^yDu$, equivalently
$u^*(y)-u^*(x)=\int_x^yDu$ whenever $x\le y$.

If $I=(a,b)$ has finite endpoints, then $Du\in L^1(a,b)$, the representative
$u^*$ extends uniquely to an absolutely continuous function on $[a,b]$, and
the extension satisfies
$$u^*(x)=u^*(a)+\int_a^xDu(t)\,dt\qquad\text{for every }x\in[a,b].$$

The scalar field is arbitrary, $p=1$ and $p=\infty$ are included, and the
one-dimensional interval may be bounded or unbounded. The Axiom of Choice is
used only through the Countable-Choice and Dependent-Choice hypotheses of the
cited characterisation, fundamental-theorem and completeness interfaces.

Let $\mathcal T$ be a cell-face mesh as in [[def-fv-admissible-cell-face-mesh]], with $x_K$ the volume centroid of each cell and $x_F$ the face centroid. For the mimetic branch require the following explicit face-moment closure on each cell:
$$ \sum_{F\subset\partial K}|F|n_{K,F}=0,\qquad \sum_{F\subset\partial K}|F|x_F\otimes n_{K,F}=|K|I_d. $$
Here $I_d$ is the identity matrix on $\mathbb R^d$ and $(x\otimes n)_{ij}=x_i n_j$. These are finite geometric checks on the face data; they impose no center-to-face orthogonality. For every cell use one real cell-mean unknown $u_K$; for every face use one shared real face-mean unknown $u_F$. On a boundary face $F\subset\partial\Omega$, the value $u_F=g_F$ is prescribed. Write $n_{K,F}$ for the outward unit normal. Define the reconstructed cell gradient and its face residual by
$$ G_Ku=\frac1{|K|}\sum_{F\subset\partial K}|F|u_Fn_{K,F},\qquad \rho_{K,F}(u)=u_F-u_K-G_Ku\cdot(x_F-x_K). $$
Interpret $u_K$ and $u_F$ as cell and face averages. For a symmetric positive-definite tensor $A_K$ constant on $K$ (so $z\cdot A_Kz>0$ for every nonzero $z$), define
$$ \mathscr A_K(u,v)=|K|(A_KG_Ku)\cdot G_Kv+\lambda_{\min}(A_K)\sum_{F\subset\partial K}\frac{|F|}{d_{K,F}}\rho_{K,F}(u)\rho_{K,F}(v), $$
where $\lambda_{\min}(A_K)>0$ is the smallest eigenvalue of $A_K$. The **linear hybrid mimetic scheme** with homogeneous Dirichlet data is to find all cell and interior-face values $u$ such that
$$ \sum_{K\in\mathcal K}\mathscr A_K(u,v)=\sum_{K\in\mathcal K}v_K\int_K f(x)\,dx $$
for every test vector $v$ whose boundary face values are zero. For each local face $F\subset\partial K$, let $\phi_{K,F}$ have face value $1$ on $F$, zero on the other faces of $K$, and cell value zero. Define the outward numerical flux $Q_{K,F}(u)=-\mathscr A_K(u,\phi_{K,F})$.

There is also a monotone $p$-growth backward-Euler extension, specified as an algebraic scheme but with no existence or convergence claim in this definition. Let $1<p<\infty$, set $p'=p/(p-1)$, and let $a(x,\xi)$ be a **Carathéodory flux**, meaning that $x\mapsto a(x,\xi)$ is measurable for each fixed $\xi$ and $\xi\mapsto a(x,\xi)$ is continuous for almost every $x$. Assume there are constants $C,\alpha>0$, a nonnegative $g\in L^{p'}(\Omega)$, and a nonnegative $h\in L^1(\Omega)$ such that, outside one null set,
$$ |a(x,\xi)|\le C(g(x)+|\xi|^{p-1}),\qquad a(x,\xi)\cdot\xi\ge\alpha|\xi|^p-h(x),\qquad (a(x,\xi)-a(x,\eta))\cdot(\xi-\eta)\ge0. $$
For each cell set $b_K(\xi)=|K|^{-1}\int_Ka(x,\xi)\,dx$, and fix $\alpha_{0,K}>0$. Put $\psi_p(s)=|s|^{p-2}s$ for $s\ne0$ and $\psi_p(0)=0$. Its spatial operator, linear in the test vector $v$, is
$$ \mathcal A_{h,K}(u;v)=|K|b_K(G_Ku)\cdot G_Kv+\alpha_{0,K}\sum_{F\subset\partial K}\frac{|F|}{d_{K,F}^{p-1}}\psi_p(\rho_{K,F}(u))\rho_{K,F}(v). $$
For this extension define $Q_{K,F}^{\rm nl}(u)=-\mathcal A_{h,K}(u;\phi_{K,F})$.
On a time partition $0=t_0<\cdots<t_N=T$, given $u^{n-1}$ and $f\in L^{p'}((0,T)\times\Omega)$, put $f_K^n=((t_n-t_{n-1})|K|)^{-1}\int_{t_{n-1}}^{t_n}\int_K f$. The backward-Euler step seeks $u^n$ with zero boundary face values satisfying
$$ \sum_{K\in\mathcal K}|K|\frac{u_K^n-u_K^{n-1}}{t_n-t_{n-1}}v_K+\sum_{K\in\mathcal K}\mathcal A_{h,K}(u^n;v)=\sum_{K\in\mathcal K}|K|f_K^n v_K $$
for every test vector with zero boundary face values. The formula specifies a candidate discrete method; solvability and convergence require separate results.

Let $\Omega\subset\mathbb R^d$ be a nonempty bounded connected Lipschitz polyhedral domain, $d\ge1$. A **regular simplicial companion family** consists of refining uniformly regular boundary-anchored cell-face meshes in [[def-fv-admissible-cell-face-mesh]], and, for each mesh, a matching simplicial subdivision $\mathcal S_h$ of its cells with the following finite geometric data and uniform constants $c,C,J>0$.

Each cell is subdivided into at most $J$ closed nondegenerate $d$-simplices. Each simplex has diameter at most $Ch$ and inradius at least $ch$, and the chosen cell point $x_K$ is a subdivision vertex. The subdivision of each cell is a fan from $x_K$ over a triangulation of its boundary, and subdivisions agree on shared faces. Each original face is a union of at most $J$ subdivision facets. In dimension one these mean the two subintervals from $x_K$ to the endpoints.

For each subdivision vertex $z$, let $\mathcal K(z)$ consist of the original cells whose closures contain $z$. This set has at most $J$ elements. For any $K,L\in\mathcal K(z)$ there is a path of at most $J$ cells in $\mathcal K(z)$, from $K$ to $L$, consecutive cells sharing an original face whose closure contains $z$. If $z\in\partial\Omega$, every $K\in\mathcal K(z)$ has such a path to a cell with a boundary face whose closure contains $z$. These are connectivity checks on finite vertex stars, not an assumption of an analytic inequality.

For shared face values $v_F$, cell values $v_K$, and homogeneous boundary values $v_F=0$, define the piecewise constant state $\Pi_hv|_K=v_K$ and
$$D_{h,p}(v)^p=\sum_K\sum_{F\subset\partial K}|F|d_{K,F}^{1-p}|v_F-v_K|^p\qquad(1<p<\infty).$$
The mean interpolator $I_hv$ has cell and face values equal to the corresponding means of a Sobolev function, with face means interpreted by the simplex trace; for $v\in W_0^{1,p}(\Omega)$ its boundary face means are zero. Define $E_hv$ to be continuous and affine on each subdivision simplex, with nodal value $|\mathcal K(z)|^{-1}\sum_{K\in\mathcal K(z)}v_K$ at an interior vertex $z$ and zero at a boundary vertex. Thus $E_h$ is an explicit linear function of the cell values; its definition does not assume its stability.

These conditions allow nonorthogonal cells. A nonempty example in every dimension is the uniform cubical partition of $(0,1)^d$, with cell centers, a fixed matching barycentric subdivision of every face, and the cones from cell centers to those face simplices. Scaling leaves finitely many simplex shapes and bounded vertex stars; coordinate adjacency connects each interior star and connects each boundary star to a boundary face. In dimension one use equal subintervals and their midpoints. Hence all the displayed constants can be chosen independently of refinement.

Assume Countable Choice. Let $1<p<\infty$ and $p'=p/(p-1)$. For each facet $F$ of
$\widehat S_d$, restriction of smooth functions extends uniquely to a
bounded linear trace map
$$\gamma_F:W^{1,p}(\widehat S_d;\mathbb R)\to L^p(F;\mathbb R).$$
For real-valued $u\in W^{1,p}(\widehat S_d)$ and
$G\in W^{1,p'}(\widehat S_d;\mathbb R^d)$, the facet traces satisfy
$$\int_{\widehat S_d}u\,\operatorname{div}G+\nabla u\cdot G\,dx =\sum_{F\subset\partial\widehat S_d}\int_F\gamma_Fu\,\gamma_FG\cdot\widehat n_F\,dS.$$
Here $\gamma_FG$ is the componentwise trace and $\widehat n_F$ is the
outward unit normal. The bounded C1-domain trace and Green theorems are not
used for the simplex.

Assume Countable Choice. For every $1\le p<\infty$ there is
$C_{d,p}<\infty$ such that for all
$u\in W^{1,p}(\widehat S_d;\mathbb R)$,
$$\|u-u_{\widehat S_d}\|_{L^p(\widehat S_d)} \le C_{d,p}|u|_{W^{1,p}(\widehat S_d)},\qquad u_{\widehat S_d}:=|\widehat S_d|^{-1}\int_{\widehat S_d}u\,dx.$$

Let $\mathcal T$ be a cell-face mesh as in [[def-fv-admissible-cell-face-mesh]], with $x_K$ the volume centroid of each cell and $x_F$ the face centroid. For the mimetic branch require the following explicit face-moment closure on each cell:
$$ \sum_{F\subset\partial K}|F|n_{K,F}=0,\qquad \sum_{F\subset\partial K}|F|x_F\otimes n_{K,F}=|K|I_d. $$
Here $I_d$ is the identity matrix on $\mathbb R^d$ and $(x\otimes n)_{ij}=x_i n_j$. These are finite geometric checks on the face data; they impose no center-to-face orthogonality. For every cell use one real cell-mean unknown $u_K$; for every face use one shared real face-mean unknown $u_F$. On a boundary face $F\subset\partial\Omega$, the value $u_F=g_F$ is prescribed. Write $n_{K,F}$ for the outward unit normal. Define the reconstructed cell gradient and its face residual by
$$ G_Ku=\frac1{|K|}\sum_{F\subset\partial K}|F|u_Fn_{K,F},\qquad \rho_{K,F}(u)=u_F-u_K-G_Ku\cdot(x_F-x_K). $$
Interpret $u_K$ and $u_F$ as cell and face averages. For a symmetric positive-definite tensor $A_K$ constant on $K$ (so $z\cdot A_Kz>0$ for every nonzero $z$), define
$$ \mathscr A_K(u,v)=|K|(A_KG_Ku)\cdot G_Kv+\lambda_{\min}(A_K)\sum_{F\subset\partial K}\frac{|F|}{d_{K,F}}\rho_{K,F}(u)\rho_{K,F}(v), $$
where $\lambda_{\min}(A_K)>0$ is the smallest eigenvalue of $A_K$. The **linear hybrid mimetic scheme** with homogeneous Dirichlet data is to find all cell and interior-face values $u$ such that
$$ \sum_{K\in\mathcal K}\mathscr A_K(u,v)=\sum_{K\in\mathcal K}v_K\int_K f(x)\,dx $$
for every test vector $v$ whose boundary face values are zero. For each local face $F\subset\partial K$, let $\phi_{K,F}$ have face value $1$ on $F$, zero on the other faces of $K$, and cell value zero. Define the outward numerical flux $Q_{K,F}(u)=-\mathscr A_K(u,\phi_{K,F})$.

There is also a monotone $p$-growth backward-Euler extension, specified as an algebraic scheme but with no existence or convergence claim in this definition. Let $1<p<\infty$, set $p'=p/(p-1)$, and let $a(x,\xi)$ be a **Carathéodory flux**, meaning that $x\mapsto a(x,\xi)$ is measurable for each fixed $\xi$ and $\xi\mapsto a(x,\xi)$ is continuous for almost every $x$. Assume there are constants $C,\alpha>0$, a nonnegative $g\in L^{p'}(\Omega)$, and a nonnegative $h\in L^1(\Omega)$ such that, outside one null set,
$$ |a(x,\xi)|\le C(g(x)+|\xi|^{p-1}),\qquad a(x,\xi)\cdot\xi\ge\alpha|\xi|^p-h(x),\qquad (a(x,\xi)-a(x,\eta))\cdot(\xi-\eta)\ge0. $$
For each cell set $b_K(\xi)=|K|^{-1}\int_Ka(x,\xi)\,dx$, and fix $\alpha_{0,K}>0$. Put $\psi_p(s)=|s|^{p-2}s$ for $s\ne0$ and $\psi_p(0)=0$. Its spatial operator, linear in the test vector $v$, is
$$ \mathcal A_{h,K}(u;v)=|K|b_K(G_Ku)\cdot G_Kv+\alpha_{0,K}\sum_{F\subset\partial K}\frac{|F|}{d_{K,F}^{p-1}}\psi_p(\rho_{K,F}(u))\rho_{K,F}(v). $$
For this extension define $Q_{K,F}^{\rm nl}(u)=-\mathcal A_{h,K}(u;\phi_{K,F})$.
On a time partition $0=t_0<\cdots<t_N=T$, given $u^{n-1}$ and $f\in L^{p'}((0,T)\times\Omega)$, put $f_K^n=((t_n-t_{n-1})|K|)^{-1}\int_{t_{n-1}}^{t_n}\int_K f$. The backward-Euler step seeks $u^n$ with zero boundary face values satisfying
$$ \sum_{K\in\mathcal K}|K|\frac{u_K^n-u_K^{n-1}}{t_n-t_{n-1}}v_K+\sum_{K\in\mathcal K}\mathcal A_{h,K}(u^n;v)=\sum_{K\in\mathcal K}|K|f_K^n v_K $$
for every test vector with zero boundary face values. The formula specifies a candidate discrete method; solvability and convergence require separate results.

For an affine function $\ell(x)=b\cdot x+c$, its cell and face averages satisfy $G_K\ell=b$ and $\rho_{K,F}(\ell)=0$ by the displayed face-moment closure. The drawing illustrates the cell and face degrees of freedom on a skew cell; no center-to-face orthogonality is assumed.

```tikz
\begin{tikzpicture}[scale=1]
  \draw[thick] (0,0) -- (2,0) -- (3,1) -- (1,1) -- cycle;
  \fill (1.5,0.5) circle (2pt) node[below] {$u_K$};
  \fill (1,0) circle (2pt) node[below] {$u_{F_1}$};
  \fill (2.5,0.5) circle (2pt) node[right] {$u_{F_2}$};
  \fill (2,1) circle (2pt) node[above] {$u_{F_3}$};
  \fill (0.5,0.5) circle (2pt) node[left] {$u_{F_4}$};
  \draw[->,blue] (1.5,0.5) -- (2.2,0.5) node[right] {$G_Ku$};
\end{tikzpicture}
```

When $p=2$, $b_K(\xi)=A_K\xi$, and $\alpha_{0,K}=\lambda_{\min}(A_K)$, the nonlinear formula agrees with the linear form above. Neither specification by itself proves solvability, a conforming $W_0^{1,p}$ reconstruction, or a mesh-uniform discrete Aubin–Lions estimate; those require separate results or hypotheses.

Assume Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ be open and bounded in one direction: there are a unit vector $e$ and $a<b$ with $a<x\cdot e<b$ for every $x\in\Omega$. Let $1\le p<\infty$. Then $\|u\|_{L^p(\Omega)}\le C(p)\,(b-a)\,\|Du\|_{L^p(\Omega)}$ for every $u\in W^{1,p}_0(\Omega;\mathbb K)$.

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $d\ge1$, let $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^d$ be a bounded open set, and let $1<p<\infty$ satisfy $p>\max(1,2d/(d+2))$. Then $W_0^{1,p}(\Omega)$ is continuously and compactly embedded in $L^2(\Omega)$. In particular, the inclusion is dense. No boundary regularity is required.

Let $(X,\mathcal A,\mu)$ be a measure space, let $p,q\in[1,\infty]$ be
conjugate exponents, and let $f,g$ be measurable real-valued functions.

1. If $1\le p<\infty$ and $q<\infty$ with $f\in\mathcal L^p(\mu)$ and
   $g\in\mathcal L^q(\mu)$, then
   $$\int |fg|\,d\mu\le\|f\|_p\|g\|_q.$$
2. If $p=1$ and $q=\infty$ with $f\in\mathcal L^1(\mu)$ and
   $g\in L^\infty(\mu)$, then
   $$\int |fg|\,d\mu\le\|f\|_1\|g\|_\infty.$$
3. If $p=\infty$ and $q=1$ with $f\in L^\infty(\mu)$ and
   $g\in\mathcal L^1(\mu)$, then
   $$\int |fg|\,d\mu\le\|f\|_\infty\|g\|_1.$$

In every case the right-hand side is finite, so $fg$ is integrable.

Conversely $j_{K,F}=\rho_{K,F}+G_Kv\cdot(x_F-x_K)$ gives $D_{h,p}\le CB_{h,p}$.

If $K,L$ share $F$, $v_K-v_L=j_{L,F}-j_{K,F}$. Along a supplied vertex-star path, the difference between $v_K$ and any other incident cell value is a sum of at most $2J$ such increments. At a boundary vertex the same telescoping ends at a zero boundary face. Hence for every simplex $S\subset\overline K$ and its vertex $z$, $|(E_hv)(z)-v_K|^p\le C\sum_{(L,F)\in\mathcal N(K)}|j_{L,F}|^p$, where $\mathcal N(K)$ is the union of the finitely many supplied paths at its vertices. These sets have bounded cardinality and bounded overlap: a cell has at most $J(d+1)$ subdivision vertices and each vertex has at most $J$ incident cells.

The scaled simplex estimates [F2] first bound the difference between the mean on a simplex and the mean on one of its facets by $Ch^{1-d/p}\|
abla z\|_{L^p(S)}$. Means on adjacent simplices differ by the sum of their differences to the shared facet mean, since their traces agree. The fan subdivision is a connected finite union of at most $J$ simplices. Telescoping between their means, and averaging over each original cell or original face, therefore gives $|(I_hz)_F-(I_hz)_K|^p\le Ch^{p-d}\int_K|
abla z|^p$. The same trace argument applies to boundary faces; zero-boundary approximation makes their means zero. Multiplication by $|F|d_{K,F}^{1-p}\asymp h^{d-p}$ and summation proves $D_{h,p}(I_hz)\le C\|
abla z\|_p$.

For smooth $z$, Gauss–Green gives $G_KI_hz=|K|^{-1}\int_K\nabla z$ exactly. On each cell Taylor expansion around its centroid and the corresponding face averages show $|(I_hz)_F-(I_hz)_K-G_KI_hz\cdot(x_F-x_K)|\le Ch^2\|D^2z\|_\infty$ under the stated centroid hypothesis. Thus for this mean interpolator the residual sum is at most $C h^p\|D^2z\|_\infty^p$, because there are $O(h^{-d})$ cells. Uniform continuity of $\nabla z$ gives the asserted gradient consistency.

Barycentric coordinates on $S$ have absolute value at most one and gradients at most $C/h$, by the inradius bound. Applying step 1.2 to $E_hv-v_K$ gives its $p$th-power $L^p(S)$ norm at most $Ch^d$ times the path sum, and its gradient norm at most $Ch^{d-p}$ times that sum. Summing with bounded overlap proves $\|E_hv-\Pi_hv\|_p\le ChD_{h,p}$ and $\|\nabla E_hv\|_p\le CD_{h,p}$. The continuous piecewise affine function vanishes on all boundary facets. Its zero extension is globally Lipschitz and has compact support: along a segment, the finite simplex pieces and the exterior zero pieces have derivative bounded by the largest simplex gradient and agree at crossings. To verify the zero-boundary closure directly, multiply by $\max(0,\min(1,k\operatorname{dist}(x,\partial\Omega)-1))$. The error and its gradient are supported in shrinking boundary layers, and $|E_hv(x)|\le L\operatorname{dist}(x,\partial\Omega)$ bounds the cutoff-gradient term by $2L$ on the layer $1/k<\operatorname{dist}(x,\partial\Omega)<2/k$. They tend to zero in $W^{1,p}$ by absolute continuity of the integral. Each cutoff is Lipschitz with compact support in $\Omega$ and can be mollified inside $\Omega$, producing smooth compactly supported approximants. Thus $E_hv\in W_0^{1,p}$, and [F4] proves the full $W^{1,p}$ bound and the $L^p$ state bound.

For $p<2$, the same barycentric estimate in $L^2(S)$ and $\ell^2\le\ell^p$ for the combined finite coefficient list give $\|E_hv-\Pi_hv\|_2\le Ch^{d/2}(\sum_{K,F}|j_{K,F}|^p)^{1/p}\le Ch^{1+d/2-d/p}D_{h,p}$. For $p\ge2$, finite-measure Hölder and step 2.1 give $ChD_{h,p}$ instead. The exponent is positive precisely on the stated strict branch. The continuous embedding [F4] bounds $\|E_hv\|_2$, proving the state $L^2$ estimate as well.

Let $\phi_K$ and $\phi_F$ denote vector means over cells and faces. Gauss–Green, shared face cancellation and $v_F=0$ on the boundary give exactly $\int G_hv\cdot\phi+\Pi_hv\operatorname{div}\phi=\sum_{K,F}|F|j_{K,F}n_{K,F}\cdot(\phi_K-\phi_F)$. Since $|\phi_K-\phi_F|\le Ch\|
abla\phi\|_\infty$, Hölder bounds this by $ChD_{h,p}(\sum_{K,F}|F|d_{K,F})^{1/p'}\|
abla\phi\|_\infty$. The last sum is uniformly bounded by [F1], proving the estimate. Strong and weak convergence pass its left side to $\int g\cdot\phi+v\operatorname{div}\phi$, which is zero; interior compactly supported tests identify $g=
abla v$. Hölder in time gives the same assertions for space-time bounds.

Orthogonality makes their volumes $|P_{K,F}|=|F|d_{K,F}/d$, so $|\mathcal D_F|=|F|d_F/d$. Multiplying each squared reconstruction value by its physical region volume gives exactly the displayed norm identity, and [F1] proves its bound.

Let $\phi$ be any smooth vector field on a neighborhood of $\overline\Omega$, and write $\phi_F$ for its face mean. The face-oriented finite sum $\sum_{F=K|L}|F|(v_L-v_K)n_{K,F}\cdot\phi_F-\sum_{F\in\mathcal F_{\rm bdy}}|F|v_Kn_{K,F}\cdot\phi_F$ is exactly $-\int_\Omega\Pi_hv\,\operatorname{div}\phi$, by the divergence formula in each cell and face cancellation. Replacing each $\phi_F$ by the mean of $\phi$ over the corresponding diamond or boundary pyramid changes this sum by at most $Ch\|\nabla\phi\|_\infty\sum_F|F||\Delta_Fv|$. Cauchy–Schwarz bounds that last face sum by $D_{h,2}(v)(\sum_F|F|d_F)^{1/2}$, taking boundary $d_F=d_{K,F}$. The second factor equals $(d|\Omega|)^{1/2}$. By step 2.2 the modified sum is $\int\mathcal G_hv\cdot\phi$. Hence the weak-gradient defect tends to zero.

The norm bound in step 2.2 supplies a weakly convergent subsequence of physical gradients. Steps 2.1 and 3.1 identify its distributional limit as $\nabla v$. Smooth compactly supported tests determine the $L^2$ field uniquely, so every weak subsequence on the extracted state subsequence has that limit, giving the asserted weak convergence.

Assume the Axiom of Choice and a family in [[def-fv-regular-simplicial-companion-family]]. For $1<p<\infty$ and zero boundary face values, put
$$B_{h,p}(v)^p=\sum_K|K||G_Kv|^p+S_{h,p}(v)^p,\qquad S_{h,p}(v)^p=\sum_{K,F}|F|d_{K,F}^{1-p}|\rho_{K,F}(v)|^p,$$
where $G_K,\rho_{K,F}$ have the formulas in [[def-hybrid-mimetic-fv-scheme]]. Then, with constants independent of $h,v$,
$$C^{-1}D_{h,p}(v)\le B_{h,p}(v)\le CD_{h,p}(v),\quad \|E_hv\|_{W^{1,p}}\le CD_{h,p}(v),\quad \|\Pi_hv-E_hv\|_{L^p}\le ChD_{h,p}(v).$$
Here $E_hv\in W_0^{1,p}(\Omega)$. If $p>\max(1,2d/(d+2))$ and $\vartheta=1-d\max(1/p-1/2,0)>0$, also
$$\|\Pi_hv-E_hv\|_2\le Ch^\vartheta D_{h,p}(v),\qquad \|\Pi_hv\|_2+\|\Pi_hv\|_p\le CD_{h,p}(v).$$
For $z\in W_0^{1,p}(\Omega)$, $D_{h,p}(I_hz)\le C\|\nabla z\|_p$. If the cell points are volume centroids, then for smooth $z$ with compact support in $\Omega$, $G_h I_hz\to\nabla z$ uniformly and $S_{h,p}(I_hz)\le Ch\|D^2z\|_\infty$, where $G_hv|_K=G_Kv$. Finally, for every smooth vector field $\phi$ on a neighborhood of $\overline\Omega$,
$$\left|\int_\Omega G_hv\cdot\phi+\Pi_hv\,\operatorname{div}\phi\right|\le ChD_{h,p}(v)\|\nabla\phi\|_\infty.$$
Consequently bounded $D_{h,p}(v_h)$, strong $L^p$ convergence $\Pi_hv_h\to v$, and weak $L^p$ convergence $G_hv_h\rightharpoonup g$ imply $g=\nabla v$ distributionally. The same statements hold after integration in time with the corresponding $L^p$ bounds.

Let $\mathcal T$ be a cell-face mesh as in [[def-fv-admissible-cell-face-mesh]], with $x_K$ the volume centroid of each cell and $x_F$ the face centroid. For the mimetic branch require the following explicit face-moment closure on each cell:
$$ \sum_{F\subset\partial K}|F|n_{K,F}=0,\qquad \sum_{F\subset\partial K}|F|x_F\otimes n_{K,F}=|K|I_d. $$
Here $I_d$ is the identity matrix on $\mathbb R^d$ and $(x\otimes n)_{ij}=x_i n_j$. These are finite geometric checks on the face data; they impose no center-to-face orthogonality. For every cell use one real cell-mean unknown $u_K$; for every face use one shared real face-mean unknown $u_F$. On a boundary face $F\subset\partial\Omega$, the value $u_F=g_F$ is prescribed. Write $n_{K,F}$ for the outward unit normal. Define the reconstructed cell gradient and its face residual by
$$ G_Ku=\frac1{|K|}\sum_{F\subset\partial K}|F|u_Fn_{K,F},\qquad \rho_{K,F}(u)=u_F-u_K-G_Ku\cdot(x_F-x_K). $$
Interpret $u_K$ and $u_F$ as cell and face averages. For a symmetric positive-definite tensor $A_K$ constant on $K$ (so $z\cdot A_Kz>0$ for every nonzero $z$), define
$$ \mathscr A_K(u,v)=|K|(A_KG_Ku)\cdot G_Kv+\lambda_{\min}(A_K)\sum_{F\subset\partial K}\frac{|F|}{d_{K,F}}\rho_{K,F}(u)\rho_{K,F}(v), $$
where $\lambda_{\min}(A_K)>0$ is the smallest eigenvalue of $A_K$. The **linear hybrid mimetic scheme** with homogeneous Dirichlet data is to find all cell and interior-face values $u$ such that
$$ \sum_{K\in\mathcal K}\mathscr A_K(u,v)=\sum_{K\in\mathcal K}v_K\int_K f(x)\,dx $$
for every test vector $v$ whose boundary face values are zero. For each local face $F\subset\partial K$, let $\phi_{K,F}$ have face value $1$ on $F$, zero on the other faces of $K$, and cell value zero. Define the outward numerical flux $Q_{K,F}(u)=-\mathscr A_K(u,\phi_{K,F})$.

There is also a monotone $p$-growth backward-Euler extension, specified as an algebraic scheme but with no existence or convergence claim in this definition. Let $1<p<\infty$, set $p'=p/(p-1)$, and let $a(x,\xi)$ be a **Carathéodory flux**, meaning that $x\mapsto a(x,\xi)$ is measurable for each fixed $\xi$ and $\xi\mapsto a(x,\xi)$ is continuous for almost every $x$. Assume there are constants $C,\alpha>0$, a nonnegative $g\in L^{p'}(\Omega)$, and a nonnegative $h\in L^1(\Omega)$ such that, outside one null set,
$$ |a(x,\xi)|\le C(g(x)+|\xi|^{p-1}),\qquad a(x,\xi)\cdot\xi\ge\alpha|\xi|^p-h(x),\qquad (a(x,\xi)-a(x,\eta))\cdot(\xi-\eta)\ge0. $$
For each cell set $b_K(\xi)=|K|^{-1}\int_Ka(x,\xi)\,dx$, and fix $\alpha_{0,K}>0$. Put $\psi_p(s)=|s|^{p-2}s$ for $s\ne0$ and $\psi_p(0)=0$. Its spatial operator, linear in the test vector $v$, is
$$ \mathcal A_{h,K}(u;v)=|K|b_K(G_Ku)\cdot G_Kv+\alpha_{0,K}\sum_{F\subset\partial K}\frac{|F|}{d_{K,F}^{p-1}}\psi_p(\rho_{K,F}(u))\rho_{K,F}(v). $$
For this extension define $Q_{K,F}^{\rm nl}(u)=-\mathcal A_{h,K}(u;\phi_{K,F})$.
On a time partition $0=t_0<\cdots<t_N=T$, given $u^{n-1}$ and $f\in L^{p'}((0,T)\times\Omega)$, put $f_K^n=((t_n-t_{n-1})|K|)^{-1}\int_{t_{n-1}}^{t_n}\int_K f$. The backward-Euler step seeks $u^n$ with zero boundary face values satisfying
$$ \sum_{K\in\mathcal K}|K|\frac{u_K^n-u_K^{n-1}}{t_n-t_{n-1}}v_K+\sum_{K\in\mathcal K}\mathcal A_{h,K}(u^n;v)=\sum_{K\in\mathcal K}|K|f_K^n v_K $$
for every test vector with zero boundary face values. The formula specifies a candidate discrete method; solvability and convergence require separate results.

For an affine function $\ell(x)=b\cdot x+c$, its cell and face averages satisfy $G_K\ell=b$ and $\rho_{K,F}(\ell)=0$ by the displayed face-moment closure. The drawing illustrates the cell and face degrees of freedom on a skew cell; no center-to-face orthogonality is assumed.

```tikz
\begin{tikzpicture}[scale=1]
  \draw[thick] (0,0) -- (2,0) -- (3,1) -- (1,1) -- cycle;
  \fill (1.5,0.5) circle (2pt) node[below] {$u_K$};
  \fill (1,0) circle (2pt) node[below] {$u_{F_1}$};
  \fill (2.5,0.5) circle (2pt) node[right] {$u_{F_2}$};
  \fill (2,1) circle (2pt) node[above] {$u_{F_3}$};
  \fill (0.5,0.5) circle (2pt) node[left] {$u_{F_4}$};
  \draw[->,blue] (1.5,0.5) -- (2.2,0.5) node[right] {$G_Ku$};
\end{tikzpicture}
```

When $p=2$, $b_K(\xi)=A_K\xi$, and $\alpha_{0,K}=\lambda_{\min}(A_K)$, the nonlinear formula agrees with the linear form above. Neither specification by itself proves solvability, a conforming $W_0^{1,p}$ reconstruction, or a mesh-uniform discrete Aubin–Lions estimate; those require separate results or hypotheses.

Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]).

Let $d\ge1$, let $\Omega\subset\mathbb R^d$ be a bounded open set, and
let $1<p<\infty$ satisfy $p>\max(1,2d/(d+2))$. Put
$V=W_0^{1,p}(\Omega;\mathbb R)$ with norm
$\|v\|_V=\|\nabla v\|_{L^p(\Omega)}$, $H=L^2(\Omega;\mathbb R)$, and
$p'=p/(p-1)$. The Poincaré inequality makes this norm equivalent to the full
$W^{1,p}$ norm. [[lem-pe12-w0p-separable-reflexive]] gives separability and
reflexivity, while [[lem-pe12-w1p-compact-l2-embedding]] gives the dense
continuous compact inclusion $V\Subset H$; these are the hypotheses of the
evolution triple in [[def-pe12-gelfand-triple]]. The compact-inclusion result
uses the stated threshold also when $d=1$, where it reduces to $p>1$.

A measurable flux $a:\Omega\times\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R^d$ is an admissible
**coercive monotone diffusion flux of p-growth** if it is Carathéodory (for
each $\xi$, $x\mapsto a(x,\xi)$ is measurable, and for almost every $x$,
$\xi\mapsto a(x,\xi)$ is continuous), and there are constants $C<\infty$,
$\alpha>0$, nonnegative functions $g\in L^{p'}(\Omega)$ and
$h\in L^1(\Omega)$, and one
null set outside which, for all $\xi,\eta\in\mathbb R^d$,
$$|a(x,\xi)|\le C\bigl(g(x)+|\xi|^{p-1}\bigr),\qquad a(x,\xi)\cdot\xi\ge\alpha|\xi|^p-h(x),$$
$$\bigl(a(x,\xi)-a(x,\eta)\bigr)\cdot(\xi-\eta)\ge0.$$
The induced operator $A:V\to V^*$ is
$$\langle A(v),w\rangle_{V^*,V} =\int_\Omega a(x,\nabla v(x))\cdot\nabla w(x)\,dx.$$
The growth bound and Hölder's inequality make this pairing finite and give
$\|A(v)\|_{V^*}\le C_1(\|g\|_{p'}+\|v\|_V^{p-1})$ for a constant $C_1$.
The finite-dimensional test-coordinate continuity used in the backward Euler
existence argument follows from the stated Carathéodory and growth conditions
by dominated convergence, as proved in
[[thm-pe12-backward-euler-galerkin-existence-energy]]. No additional global
operator-continuity hypothesis is imposed.

For $f\in L^{p'}(0,T;V^*)$, a weak evolution solution is a function
$u\in W_p(0,T;V)\cap L^\infty(0,T;H)$ with a continuous $H$ representative
such that $u'+A(u)=f$ in $L^{p'}(0,T;V^*)$ and $u(0)=u_0\in H$.

Let $N\ge1$, $R>0$, and let $F:\mathbb R^N\to\mathbb R^N$ be continuous.
If $F(x)\cdot x>0$ for every $|x|=R$, then $F$ has a zero in the closed
ball $\overline B_R(0)$.

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $d\ge1$, let $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^d$ be a bounded open set, and let $1<p<\infty$ satisfy $p>\max(1,2d/(d+2))$. Then $W_0^{1,p}(\Omega)$ is continuously and compactly embedded in $L^2(\Omega)$. In particular, the inclusion is dense. No boundary regularity is required.

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $n\ge1$, let $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ be a
bounded open set and let $1\le p<\infty$. Then $W^{1,p}_0(\Omega)$ is
compactly embedded in $L^p(\Omega)$: the inclusion is bounded, and every
sequence bounded in $W^{1,p}_0(\Omega)$ has a subsequence converging in
$L^p(\Omega)$. No regularity of $\partial\Omega$ is needed.

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let
$\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^d$ be bounded and open, $d\ge1$, let
$1<p<\infty$, and let $0<T<\infty$. Put $V=W_0^{1,p}(\Omega;\mathbb R)$ with gradient norm
$\|v\|_V=\|\nabla v\|_{L^p}$, and suppose $V$ has a continuous inclusion in
a real Hilbert space $H$. If $u_j$ is bounded in $L^p(0,T;V)$ and its image
in $L^p(0,T;H)$ converges strongly to $u$, then a subsequence converges
weakly in $L^p(0,T;V)$ to some $U$, the image of $U$ equals $u$, and
$\nabla u_j\rightharpoonup\nabla U$ in
$L^p((0,T)\times\Omega;\mathbb R^d)$.

Assume the Axiom of Choice.

Let $V\Subset H\hookrightarrow V^*$ be a Banach evolution triple. For each
$k$, let $0=t_0^k<\cdots<t_{N_k}^k=T$ be a partition with maximum step
$\delta_k\to0$, let $U_k^n\in V$, and define $\overline U_k(t)=U_k^n$ on
$I_n^k=(t_{n-1}^k,t_n^k]$ and
$D_k(t)=(U_k^n-U_k^{n-1})/\tau_n^k$ there. Suppose, for some
$1<p<\infty$ and $1<q\le\infty$,
$$\sup_k\|\overline U_k\|_{L^p(0,T;V)} +\sup_k\|D_k\|_{L^q(0,T;V^*)}<\infty.$$
Then the time translates satisfy, on their common intervals,
$$\|\overline U_k(\cdot+s)-\overline U_k\|_{L^q(V^*)} \le (s+2\delta_k)\|D_k\|_{L^q(V^*)},$$
and $(\overline U_k)$ is relatively compact in $L^p(0,T;H)$. If also
$\sup_{k,n}\|U_k^n\|_H<\infty$, every convergent subsequence converges in
every $L^r(0,T;H)$ with $1\le r<\infty$.

Let $(X,\mathcal A,\mu)$ be a measure space, let $p,q\in[1,\infty]$ be
conjugate exponents, and let $f,g$ be measurable real-valued functions.

1. If $1\le p<\infty$ and $q<\infty$ with $f\in\mathcal L^p(\mu)$ and
   $g\in\mathcal L^q(\mu)$, then
   $$\int |fg|\,d\mu\le\|f\|_p\|g\|_q.$$
2. If $p=1$ and $q=\infty$ with $f\in\mathcal L^1(\mu)$ and
   $g\in L^\infty(\mu)$, then
   $$\int |fg|\,d\mu\le\|f\|_1\|g\|_\infty.$$
3. If $p=\infty$ and $q=1$ with $f\in L^\infty(\mu)$ and
   $g\in\mathcal L^1(\mu)$, then
   $$\int |fg|\,d\mu\le\|f\|_\infty\|g\|_1.$$

In every case the right-hand side is finite, so $fg$ is integrable.

Let $(X,\mathcal A,\mu)$ be an arbitrary measure space. All functions below have domain $X$. Let $f$ and $(f_n)$ be measurable complex-valued functions such that
$f_n\to f$ almost everywhere and $|f_n|\le g$ almost everywhere for a single
nonnegative measurable function $g$ with $\int g\,d\mu<+\infty$. Then
$f\in L^1(\mu)$,
$$\int|f_n-f|\,d\mu\longrightarrow0,$$
and hence
$$\int f_n\,d\mu\longrightarrow\int f\,d\mu.$$

derivations.claim: The quantity $B_{h,p}$ is a norm on the finite zero-boundary cell-face space: if it vanishes, $G_K=0$ and $\rho_{K,F}=0$, so $v_K=v_F$; connectedness and the boundary faces force every value to zero. Coercivity in [F2] and the lower stabilization bound give $\sum_K\mathcal A_{h,K}(v;v)\ge c B_{h,p}(v)^p-\|h_0\|_1$, writing $h_0$ for the flux's coercivity datum. At a fixed step the mass term paired with $v$ is bounded below by $-C_h\|\Pi_hU^{n-1}\|_2 B_{h,p}(v)$, and the source term is at most $C\|f^n\|_{p'}B_{h,p}(v)$ by [F1]. The averaged cell flux is continuous in its finite-dimensional arguments by its growth bound and dominated convergence on bounded argument sets. Thus the equation's coordinate residual is continuous and its pairing with $v$ is positive on every sufficiently large Euclidean sphere, since finite-dimensional norm equivalence and $p>1$ make the $B_{h,p}^p$ term dominate the linear terms. Brouwer [F2] gives a solution, inductively at every step. No mesh-uniform sphere radius is needed for existence.

Test each step by $U^n$ and use $2(a-b)a=a^2-b^2+(a-b)^2$ in the volume-weighted cell inner product. Hölder and [F1] bound the source by $C\|f^n\|_{p'}B_{h,p}(U^n)$, which is at most $(c/2)B_{h,p}(U^n)^p+C\|f^n\|_{p'}^{p'}$: this scalar Young bound follows by maximizing $xy-(c/2)y^p$ over $y\ge0$. Multiply by $\tau_n$ and sum to any terminal index. Jensen for the cell/time averages gives $\sum_n\tau_n\|f^n\|_{p'}^{p'}\le\|f\|_{L^{p'}(Q)}^{p'}$. Coercivity contributes at worst $T\|h_0\|_1$. The initial norms are bounded by strong initialization, giving all three displayed energy bounds and the $L^p$ bound on $B_{h,p}$.

For $z\in V$, test a time step by $I_hz$. Because its cell values are the exact cell means, the mass term is exactly $\int_\Omega D_t(\Pi_hU^n)z$ and the load is exactly $\int_\Omega f^nz$. Growth and Hölder give $|\sum_K\mathcal A_{h,K}(U^n;I_hz)|\le C(\|g\|_{p'}+B_{h,p}(U^n)^{p-1})\|z\|_V$: the flux term uses $\|G_hI_hz\|_p\le C\|z\|_V$, and the stabilization term uses its weighted Hölder bound $C S_{h,p}(U^n)^{p-1}S_{h,p}(I_hz)$. Hence $\|D_t\Pi_hU^n\|_{V^*}\le C(\|f^n\|_{p'}+\|g\|_{p'}+B_{h,p}(U^n)^{p-1})$. Since $(p-1)p'=p$, step 2.1 gives the asserted derivative bound for the affine cell-state interpolation.

Fix $\varepsilon>0$. Compactness $V\Subset H$ gives a finite-dimensional subspace $Z\subset V$ and its $H$-orthogonal projection $P_Z$ such that $\|(I-P_Z)v\|_H\le\varepsilon\|v\|_V$ for all $v\in V$: take a finite $\varepsilon$-net of the $V$ unit ball's image and span its centers. By [F1], $\|(I-P_Z)\Pi_h\overline U_h\|_{L^p(H)}\le C(h^\vartheta+\varepsilon)$. Each coefficient $(\Pi_hU^n,z)_H$, $z$ in a fixed orthonormal basis of $Z$, is bounded uniformly in $n$ by step 2.1, and its affine interpolant has derivative bounded in $L^{p'}$ by step 3.1. Hölder gives its common modulus $C|t-s|^{1/p}$. Finite-grid rounding therefore makes these finitely many coefficients totally bounded in the uniform norm. Their largest nodal jumps are at most $C\delta_h^{1/p}$, so the piecewise constant coefficients have the same compactness. The projection remainder tends to zero as first $h\to0$ and then $\varepsilon\downarrow0$. Completeness of $L^p(H)$ and AC extract strong convergence there. This proves compactness for the actual cell states without falsely applying a conforming-state theorem to them.

The companions differ from the cell states by $Ch^\vartheta$ in $L^p(H)$ and are bounded in $L^p(V)$. Thus [F3] gives $u\in L^p(V)$ and weak companion convergence. The uniform cell-state $L^\infty(H)$ bound passes to $u$ by almost-everywhere $H$ convergence along a further subsequence. It upgrades strong $L^p(H)$ convergence to every finite $L^r(H)$: finite-measure Hölder treats $r<p$, while $\|v_h-u\|_{L^r(H)}^r\le(2M)^{r-p}\|v_h-u\|_{L^p(H)}^p$ treats $r\ge p$. The bounded fields $G_h\overline U_h$ have weak $L^p$ subsequences; the weak-gradient defect in [F1], integrated in time, identifies every such limit as $\nabla u$.

Compactness $V\Subset L^p$ and continuous $V\to H$ give for each $\varepsilon>0$ an Ehrling estimate $\|z\|_p\le\varepsilon\|z\|_V+C_\varepsilon\|z\|_H$. Indeed, if this failed, normalize counterexamples to $\|z_j\|_p=1$, with $\|z_j\|_V\le1/\varepsilon$ and $\|z_j\|_H\to0$. Compactness in $L^p$ gives a limit of norm one, while the $H$ convergence makes that limit zero as a distribution, a contradiction. Apply this estimate to $E_h\overline U_h-u$, whose $L^p(V)$ norm is bounded and whose $L^p(H)$ norm tends to zero. It tends to zero in $L^p(Q)$ after $h\to0$ and then $\varepsilon\downarrow0$. Its $L^p(Q)$ distance from $\Pi_h\overline U_h$ is $O(h)$ by [F1]. This proves the remaining strong convergence. All arguments used only $h\to0$ and $\delta_h\to0$ separately.

Initial face values can be set arbitrarily because only initial cell values occur in the time term.

On arbitrary time partitions with maximum step $\delta_h\to0$, every selection of step solutions satisfies, uniformly in $h$,
$$\max_n\|\Pi_hU_h^n\|_2^2+\sum_n\|\Pi_h(U_h^n-U_h^{n-1})\|_2^2+\sum_n\tau_n B_{h,p}(U_h^n)^p\le C.$$

The piecewise affine interpolation of $\Pi_hU_h^n$ has derivative bounded in $L^{p'}(0,T;V^*)$, $V=W_0^{1,p}(\Omega)$. There are a subsequence and $u\in L^p(0,T;V)\cap L^\infty(0,T;H)$ such that
$$\Pi_h\overline U_h\to u\text{ in }L^r(0,T;H)\ (1\le r<\infty)\text{ and in }L^p(Q),$$
$$E_h\overline U_h\rightharpoonup u\text{ in }L^p(0,T;V),\qquad G_h\overline U_h\rightharpoonup\nabla u\text{ in }L^p(Q;\mathbb R^d).$$
No mesh/time coupling or time-step ratio restriction is required.

Assume the Axiom of Choice and a family in [[def-fv-regular-simplicial-companion-family]]. For $1<p<\infty$ and zero boundary face values, put
$$B_{h,p}(v)^p=\sum_K|K||G_Kv|^p+S_{h,p}(v)^p,\qquad S_{h,p}(v)^p=\sum_{K,F}|F|d_{K,F}^{1-p}|\rho_{K,F}(v)|^p,$$
where $G_K,\rho_{K,F}$ have the formulas in [[def-hybrid-mimetic-fv-scheme]]. Then, with constants independent of $h,v$,
$$C^{-1}D_{h,p}(v)\le B_{h,p}(v)\le CD_{h,p}(v),\quad \|E_hv\|_{W^{1,p}}\le CD_{h,p}(v),\quad \|\Pi_hv-E_hv\|_{L^p}\le ChD_{h,p}(v).$$
Here $E_hv\in W_0^{1,p}(\Omega)$. If $p>\max(1,2d/(d+2))$ and $\vartheta=1-d\max(1/p-1/2,0)>0$, also
$$\|\Pi_hv-E_hv\|_2\le Ch^\vartheta D_{h,p}(v),\qquad \|\Pi_hv\|_2+\|\Pi_hv\|_p\le CD_{h,p}(v).$$
For $z\in W_0^{1,p}(\Omega)$, $D_{h,p}(I_hz)\le C\|\nabla z\|_p$. If the cell points are volume centroids, then for smooth $z$ with compact support in $\Omega$, $G_h I_hz\to\nabla z$ uniformly and $S_{h,p}(I_hz)\le Ch\|D^2z\|_\infty$, where $G_hv|_K=G_Kv$. Finally, for every smooth vector field $\phi$ on a neighborhood of $\overline\Omega$,
$$\left|\int_\Omega G_hv\cdot\phi+\Pi_hv\,\operatorname{div}\phi\right|\le ChD_{h,p}(v)\|\nabla\phi\|_\infty.$$
Consequently bounded $D_{h,p}(v_h)$, strong $L^p$ convergence $\Pi_hv_h\to v$, and weak $L^p$ convergence $G_hv_h\rightharpoonup g$ imply $g=\nabla v$ distributionally. The same statements hold after integration in time with the corresponding $L^p$ bounds.

Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]).

Let $d\ge1$, let $\Omega\subset\mathbb R^d$ be a bounded open set, and
let $1<p<\infty$ satisfy $p>\max(1,2d/(d+2))$. Put
$V=W_0^{1,p}(\Omega;\mathbb R)$ with norm
$\|v\|_V=\|\nabla v\|_{L^p(\Omega)}$, $H=L^2(\Omega;\mathbb R)$, and
$p'=p/(p-1)$. The Poincaré inequality makes this norm equivalent to the full
$W^{1,p}$ norm. [[lem-pe12-w0p-separable-reflexive]] gives separability and
reflexivity, while [[lem-pe12-w1p-compact-l2-embedding]] gives the dense
continuous compact inclusion $V\Subset H$; these are the hypotheses of the
evolution triple in [[def-pe12-gelfand-triple]]. The compact-inclusion result
uses the stated threshold also when $d=1$, where it reduces to $p>1$.

A measurable flux $a:\Omega\times\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R^d$ is an admissible
**coercive monotone diffusion flux of p-growth** if it is Carathéodory (for
each $\xi$, $x\mapsto a(x,\xi)$ is measurable, and for almost every $x$,
$\xi\mapsto a(x,\xi)$ is continuous), and there are constants $C<\infty$,
$\alpha>0$, nonnegative functions $g\in L^{p'}(\Omega)$ and
$h\in L^1(\Omega)$, and one
null set outside which, for all $\xi,\eta\in\mathbb R^d$,
$$|a(x,\xi)|\le C\bigl(g(x)+|\xi|^{p-1}\bigr),\qquad a(x,\xi)\cdot\xi\ge\alpha|\xi|^p-h(x),$$
$$\bigl(a(x,\xi)-a(x,\eta)\bigr)\cdot(\xi-\eta)\ge0.$$
The induced operator $A:V\to V^*$ is
$$\langle A(v),w\rangle_{V^*,V} =\int_\Omega a(x,\nabla v(x))\cdot\nabla w(x)\,dx.$$
The growth bound and Hölder's inequality make this pairing finite and give
$\|A(v)\|_{V^*}\le C_1(\|g\|_{p'}+\|v\|_V^{p-1})$ for a constant $C_1$.
The finite-dimensional test-coordinate continuity used in the backward Euler
existence argument follows from the stated Carathéodory and growth conditions
by dominated convergence, as proved in
[[thm-pe12-backward-euler-galerkin-existence-energy]]. No additional global
operator-continuity hypothesis is imposed.

For $f\in L^{p'}(0,T;V^*)$, a weak evolution solution is a function
$u\in W_p(0,T;V)\cap L^\infty(0,T;H)$ with a continuous $H$ representative
such that $u'+A(u)=f$ in $L^{p'}(0,T;V^*)$ and $u(0)=u_0\in H$.

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let
$(V,H,J)$ be the Banach evolution triple of
[[def-pe12-gelfand-triple]], let $1<p<\infty$, and suppose
$u\in L^p(0,T;V)$ with distributional derivative
$u'\in L^{p'}(0,T;V^*)$. Then $u$ has a unique representative in
$C([0,T];H)$ and, for every $0\le s\le t\le T$,
$$\|u(t)\|_H^2-\|u(s)\|_H^2 =2\int_s^t\langle u'(r),u(r)\rangle_{V^*,V}\,dr.$$

Assume the Axiom of Choice.

Let $Q=(0,T)\times\Omega$ have finite measure, $1<p<\infty$, and let
$a(x,\xi)$ be a Carathéodory flux with the monotonicity and $p$-growth
hypotheses of [[def-pe12-monotone-diffusion-flux]], independent of time.
Suppose $\xi_n\rightharpoonup\xi$ in $L^p(Q;\mathbb R^d)$,
$q_n=a(x,\xi_n)\rightharpoonup q$ in $L^{p'}(Q;\mathbb R^d)$, and
$$\limsup_{n\to\infty}\int_Q q_n\cdot\xi_n \le\int_Qq\cdot\xi.$$
Then $q(x,t)=a(x,\xi(x,t))$ for almost every $(t,x)\in Q$.

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $\Omega\subset\mathbb R^d$ be bounded and open, $d\ge1$, let $p>\max(1,2d/(d+2))$, put $p'=p/(p-1)$, $V=W_0^{1,p}(\Omega;\mathbb R)$ with gradient norm, $H=L^2(\Omega;\mathbb R)$, and $Q=(0,T)\times\Omega$ for $T>0$. Let $a(x,\xi)$ satisfy the Carathéodory, $p$-growth, coercivity, and monotonicity hypotheses of [[def-pe12-monotone-diffusion-flux]].

For each $m$, let $\mathcal P_m$ be a finite measurable partition of $\Omega$ into cells of positive measure and let a finite time partition carry cell values. Let $\bar U_m$ be the function constant on each resulting space-time cell. Suppose there are conforming reconstructions $w_m\in L^p(0,T;V)$ and a function $u\in L^p(0,T;V)\cap L^\infty(0,T;H)$ such that
$$ \bar U_m\to u\text{ strongly in }L^p(0,T;H),\qquad \|\bar U_m-w_m\|_{L^p(0,T;H)}\to0, $$
and $\sup_m\|w_m\|_{L^p(0,T;V)}<\infty$. Write $\xi_m=\nabla w_m$ and $q_m=a(x,\xi_m)$. Assume, along the same subsequence, $q_m\rightharpoonup q$ in $L^{p'}(Q;\mathbb R^d)$ and
$$ \limsup_{m\to\infty}\int_Qq_m\cdot\xi_m\le\int_Qq\cdot\nabla u. $$
Finally, assume $f\in L^{p'}(Q)$, $u_0\in H$, and the finite-volume weak identities have residuals $r_m(\varphi)\to0$ for every $\varphi\in C_c^\infty([0,T)\times\Omega)$:
$$ -\int_Q\bar U_m\,\partial_t\varphi+\int_Qq_m\cdot\nabla\varphi-\int_Qf\varphi-\int_\Omega u_0(x)\varphi(x,0)\,dx=r_m(\varphi). $$
Then $q=a(x,\nabla u)$ almost everywhere, and $u$ is a weak evolution solution of $u_t-\operatorname{div}(a(x,\nabla u))=f$ with initial trace $u(0)=u_0$, in the sense of [[def-pe12-monotone-diffusion-flux]]:
$$ -\int_Q u\,\partial_t\varphi+\int_Qa(x,\nabla u)\cdot\nabla\varphi=\int_Qf\varphi+\int_\Omega u_0(x)\varphi(x,0)\,dx $$
for every such test function. This is a conditional finite-volume limit-identification result; the reconstruction, residual, compactness, and energy hypotheses are not conclusions of the statement.

Let $(X,\mathcal A,\mu)$ be a measure space, let $p,q\in[1,\infty]$ be
conjugate exponents, and let $f,g$ be measurable real-valued functions.

1. If $1\le p<\infty$ and $q<\infty$ with $f\in\mathcal L^p(\mu)$ and
   $g\in\mathcal L^q(\mu)$, then
   $$\int |fg|\,d\mu\le\|f\|_p\|g\|_q.$$
2. If $p=1$ and $q=\infty$ with $f\in\mathcal L^1(\mu)$ and
   $g\in L^\infty(\mu)$, then
   $$\int |fg|\,d\mu\le\|f\|_1\|g\|_\infty.$$
3. If $p=\infty$ and $q=1$ with $f\in L^\infty(\mu)$ and
   $g\in\mathcal L^1(\mu)$, then
   $$\int |fg|\,d\mu\le\|f\|_\infty\|g\|_1.$$

In every case the right-hand side is finite, so $fg$ is integrable.

**Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$.**  For every
measure space $(S,\mathcal A,\mu)$ and every $1<p<\infty$, both
$L^p(\mu;\mathbb R)$ and $L^p(\mu;\mathbb C)$ are reflexive.

Assume the ultrafilter lemma, DC, and HB.  A real or complex Banach space $X$
is reflexive if and only if every norm-bounded sequence in $X$ has a
subsequence that converges weakly to a point of $X$.

derivations.claim: Use [F1] to extract the strong cell-state and weak-gradient subsequence. Growth gives $\|q_h\|_{L^{p'}(Q)}\le C(\|g\|_{L^{p'}(Q)}+\|G_h\overline U_h\|_{L^p(Q)}^{p-1})$, so reflexive weak compactness gives $q_h\rightharpoonup q$ along a further subsequence. The cell averages $b_h$ have the same weak limit: for a smooth vector test $\phi$, $\int(q_h-b_h)\cdot\phi=\sum_{n,K}\int_{I_n\times K}q_h\cdot(\phi-\phi_K)$, whose absolute value is $O(h)\|q_h\|_{p'}\|\nabla_x\phi\|_\infty$. The averages are bounded by Jensen, and density extends this identification to all dual tests.

Let $\varphi\in C_c^\infty([0,T)\times\Omega)$. In each step test by $I_h\varphi(t_{n-1})$ and sum after multiplying by $\tau_n$. The gradient part equals $\sum_n\int_{I_n\times\Omega}q_h\cdot G_hI_h\varphi(t_{n-1})$, and replacing the last factor by $\nabla\varphi(t,x)$ costs $O(h+\delta_h)\|q_h\|_{p'}$, by smoothness and [F2]. Weighted Hölder bounds the entire stabilization part by $C\|S_{h,p}(\overline U_h)\|_{L^p}^{p-1}\|S_{h,p}(I_h\varphi(t_{n-1}))\|_{L^p}=O(h)$. Since the test cell values are exact means, discrete summation by parts in the mass term is exact. In fact the summed mass term equals $-\int_Q\Pi_h\overline U_h\partial_t\varphi-\int_\Omega\Pi_hU_h^0\varphi(0)$ exactly, since $\varphi(T)=0$ and the increment $\varphi(t_n)-\varphi(t_{n-1})$ equals its time-derivative integral on each interval. The load converges to $\int_Qf\varphi$: because its cell/time means pair exactly with a cell/time constant test, replacing that test by $\varphi$ costs $O(h+\delta_h)\|f\|_{p'}$. Consequently the actual computed fields satisfy $$-\int_Q\Pi_h\overline U_h\partial_t\varphi+\int_Qq_h\cdot\nabla\varphi-\int_Qf\varphi-\int_\Omega u_0\varphi(0)\longrightarrow0.$$ Passing to the limit gives the corresponding identity with $u,q$. This proves vanishing smooth-test residuals directly from the scheme.

The limiting identity gives $u'=f+\operatorname{div}q\in L^{p'}(0,T;V^*)$, since $|\int fz-q\cdot\nabla z|\le(C_P\|f\|_{p'}+\|q\|_{p'})\|z\|_V$. Density of smooth compactly supported functions in $V$ extends the derivative identity to all $V$ tests. Together with [F1], [F3] gives $u\in C([0,T];H)$. Scalar integration by parts in the limiting identity with tests $\theta(t)z(x)$ identifies $(u(0),z)_H=(u_0,z)_H$ for every smooth compactly supported $z$, hence $u(0)=u_0$. Its energy identity before flux identification is $$\frac12\|u(T)\|_H^2-\frac12\|u_0\|_H^2=\int_Qfu-\int_Qq\cdot\nabla u.$$

The affine interpolated scalar pairings $(\widehat{\Pi_hU_h}(t),z)_H$ for $z\in V$ have uniformly bounded $L^{p'}$ derivatives and uniform $H$ bounds by [F1]. They are equicontinuous with modulus $C_z|t-s|^{1/p}$, and their distance from the piecewise constant pairings is at most $C_z\delta_h^{1/p}$. Strong time-integrated state convergence identifies their uniform limit as $(u(t),z)_H$; finite-grid compactness followed by uniqueness of this limit justifies taking the uniform limit. At $T$ their values are $(\Pi_hU_h^{N_h},z)_H$. Density of $V$ in $H$ and the uniform terminal bound give $\Pi_hU_h^{N_h}\rightharpoonup u(T)$ in $H$. In particular $\|u(T)\|_H^2\le\liminf_h\|\Pi_hU_h^{N_h}\|_H^2$.

Testing each step by its own state and summing gives the exact identity $$\frac12\|\Pi_hU_h^{N_h}\|_H^2+\frac12\sum_n\|\Pi_h(U_h^n-U_h^{n-1})\|_H^2+\int_Qq_h\cdot G_h\overline U_h+\sum_{n,K,F}\tau_n\alpha_{0,K}|F|d_{K,F}^{1-p}|\rho_{K,F}(U_h^n)|^p=\frac12\|\Pi_hU_h^0\|_H^2+\int_Qf\Pi_h\overline U_h.$$ The load equality uses that the state is constant on each space-time cell. Its limit is $\int fu$ by strong $L^p(Q)$ convergence. The initial norms converge strongly, and all the jump and stabilization terms are nonnegative. Step 4.1 and the energy identity in step 3.1 therefore give $\limsup_h\int_Qq_h\cdot G_h\overline U_h\le\int_Qq\cdot\nabla u$. Thus [F3] applies to the actual computed $G_h\overline U_h$ and $q_h=a(x,G_h\overline U_h)$, yielding $q=a(x,\nabla u)$ almost everywhere. Steps 2.1–3.1 now give exactly the claimed weak evolution solution.

Pointwise monotonicity compared with the fixed field $
abla u$ gives $0\le\int_Q(q_h-a(x,
abla u))\cdot(G_h\overline U_h-
abla u)$. Expanding and passing through the three weakly linear terms gives $\liminf_h\int q_h\cdot G_h\overline U_h\ge\int q\cdot
abla u$, because $q=a(x,
abla u)$. Together with step 5.1 this proves energy convergence. In the exact discrete identity of step 5.1 the right side converges, the flux term now converges, and the terminal norm has the stated lower bound. Hence the sum of the nonnegative jump and stabilization terms tends to zero, and the terminal norms converge to $\|u(T)\|_H$. Weak terminal convergence plus convergence of norms in the real Hilbert space gives strong terminal convergence. The lower bound $\alpha_{0,K}\ge\underline\alpha$ proves $\sum_n	au_nS_{h,p}(U_h^n)^p	o0$.

For a local face basis, $G_K\phi_{K,F}=|F|n_{K,F}/|K|$ and $\rho_{K,E}(\phi_{K,F})=\mathbf1_{E=F}-(|F|/|K|)n_{K,F}\cdot r_{K,E}$. Substitution into the defined spatial form gives $Q_{K,F}^{\rm nl}=-|F|(b_K-c_K)\cdot n_{K,F}-s_{K,F}$, exactly the stated normal trace of $q_h^{\rm num}$. Pyramid volumes are $|F|\operatorname{dist}(x_K,\operatorname{aff}F)/d\asymp |F|h$, by the shape-regular fan geometry. Since $d_{K,F}\asymp h$, weighted finite-sum Hölder and the bounded face count give $$\int_Q|q_h^{\rm num}-b_h|^{p'}\le C\sum_{n,K,F}\tau_n|F|h^{1-p}|\rho_{K,F}(U_h^n)|^p\le C\sum_n\tau_n S_{h,p}(U_h^n)^p.$$ Indeed the $s_{K,F}/|F|$ term contributes $|F|h(h^{1-p}|\rho|^{p-1})^{p'}=|F|h^{1-p}|\rho|^p$, and $c_K=|K|^{-1}\sum_Fs_{K,F}r_{K,F}$ has the same bound after summing its cell volume. Step 6.1 proves strong vanishing of this difference. Step 1.1 gives $b_h\rightharpoonup q$, so the full numerical reconstruction converges weakly to the asserted physical flux. It need not be continuous across internal pyramid interfaces; the result asserts exactly its physical face normal values and its $L^{p'}$ weak convergence.

The weak evolution solution already established above belongs to $L^p(V)\cap L^\infty(H)$. Set $w_h=u$ on the extracted sequence and $\widetilde q_h=a(x,\nabla u)$. Strong computed-state convergence in [F1] gives $\|\Pi_h\overline U_h-w_h\|_{L^p(H)}\to0$. The conforming gradients and recovery fluxes are constant sequences, so their weak convergence and flux-energy limsup are equalities. Define the old lemma's residual using these recovery fluxes. Subtracting the exact weak equation for $u$ leaves just $-\int_Q(\Pi_h\overline U_h-u)\partial_t\varphi$, which tends to zero. Thus every old conditional hypothesis is fulfilled on the bounded open domain. This is an existential limit recovery, not a claim that the computed companion gradients converge strongly or that its nonlinear flux equals the numerical flux; steps 1.1–7.1 supplied the actual scheme closure first.
